How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Manager Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and

public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  A. REVIEW OF APPROVED ACTION PLAN

  Chair Lubisich presented the item.

  The Committee noted that approval by both chiefs was missing from the action
  plan.

  Public Comment: None

  B. FINALIZE LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT AND USES

  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  The committee decided to shorten the statement they previously developed:

  “The City of San Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded village of Sibagna. The
  City acknowledges the ancestors of this village, those collectivized at the San
  Gabriel Mission, and its responsibility to educate residents of the enduring legacy
  of this vibrant community”.

  The committee discussed the uses of the statement, including printed materials,
  creating plaques, posting it on the city website, and projecting it onto the screen
  during council meetings and events.

  The committee would like to have the tribal leaders review the statement before
  taking it back to the commissions.

  A motion was made by Vice-Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by
  Commissioner Mojarro to approve the updated version of the Land
  Acknowledgement Statement and possible uses with the clarifications provided,

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  September 13, 2023

TO:  Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  LAND ACKOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT AND USES

BACKGROUND

At the October 6, 2021 meeting the Land Acknowledgement Statement (LAS) Advisory
Committee approved a purpose statement to help guide the development of the land
acknowledgment statement. The approved statement is as follows: The Land
Acknowledgement Statement serves as a clear and ongoing commitment from the City
of San Gabriel to respect and acknowledge the native peoples of San Gabriel for their
past, current, and future contributions to the region. The committee had active
discussions with the tribal leaders to ensure the language in the statement best
represented the land and peoples it was acknowledging. At the August 11, 2022 LAS
Advisory Committee approved a land acknowledgement statement and proposed uses.
The HEAR Commission and Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission
(HPRC) have reviewed the proposal from the LAS Advisory Committee and provided
recommendations. Finally, staff collected feedback from the tribal leaders following the
February 16, 2023 meeting.

PROPOSED LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT (LAS)

“The City of San Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded village of Sibangna. The City
acknowledges the ancestors of this village, those collectivized at the San Gabriel Mission,
and its responsibility to educate residents about the enduring legacy of this vibrant
community.”

POSSIBLE USES FOR THE LAS STATEMENT

The Committee has expressed interest and a need for the City’s land acknowledgement
statement to make a larger impact than simply a statement. Below is what was developed
at the May 9 meeting.
   Land Acknowledgement Statement and Uses
  September 13, 2023
  Page 2

  •  Post on the City Website
  •  Read aloud at City meetings (alongside the pledge of allegiance) and functions and
  include on printed materials pointing to the City Website where the statement is
  listed
  •  Post at the front of the Mission Playhouse and/ or City Hall
  •  Map of the indigenous villages with the statement
  o HEAR Commission recommends adding that the map is for the education,
  distribution or posting.
  •  Recommend the San Gabriel Unified School District use the statement at events
  and include it in the California history class curriculum
  •  Initiation of education and outreach
  •  Include in the Discover San Gabriel publication
  •  Print and post for viewing at City events, including events at the Mission Playhouse
  hosted by the City

DEVELOPMENT OF ABREVIATED STATEMENT
  • The HEAR Commission at the August 23 meeting approved the full LAS as
  proposed by the LAS Advisory Committee. In addition, they are recommending the
  following:
  o Development of a shorter, more concise statement for use at meetings and
  special events. The recommended statement is as follows: “The City of San
  Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded village of Sibangna. The City
  respectfully recognizes its responsibility to the original and current
  caretakers of this land and strives to respect and honor the ancestral
  people’s legacy and educate residents of this history”.
  o HEAR Commission recommends adding that the map is for the education,
  distribution or posting.
  • The Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission (HPCRC) at the
  September 14 meeting recommends the following:
  o Shortening of the statement as proposed by the LAS to “The City of San
  Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded village of Sibangna
  acknowledging the ancestors of this village and those collectivized at the
  San Gabriel Mission. The City respectfully recognizes its responsibility to the
  enduring legacy of this vibrant community and educate residents of this
  history”. It is recommended to have a condensed statement as listed above
  rather than the full statement and an abbreviated version.
  o Ensure that the statement is used for educational purposes especially with
  relation to some of the specific words as unceded and collectivized. This
  should be included in the curriculum, especially for younger students.
   Land Acknowledgement Statement and Uses
  September 13, 2023
  Page 3

  o The map which accompanies the statement should be used more broadly
  for the planning commission as they review street names and projects within
  the City.
  •  During the February 16, 2023 Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory
  Committee meeting the committee approved the following statement and decided
  only one statement should be utilized.
  •  Since the last meeting staff met with the tribal leaders and received the following
  feedback:
  o Change from Sibangna to Tovisanga
  o Both tribal leaders wanted to see Gabrieleño included in the statement

STAFF RECCOMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee revise
and approve the statement and proposed uses.
